title: Determining Rate Laws from Initial Rates

children.text: A common experimental approach to determining rate laws is the
A common experimental approach to determine rate law expressions by measuring reaction rates when initial reactant concentrations are systematically varied.

. This method involves measuring reaction rates for multiple experimental trials using different initial reactant concentrations. Comparing the measured rates for these trials permits determination of the reaction orders and, subsequently, the rate constant. Together, the reaction orders and rate constant are used to formulate a rate law. This approach is illustrated in the next example and the following exercises.

Ozone in the upper atmosphere is depleted when it reacts with nitrogen oxides. The reaction rates of nitrogen oxides with ozone are important factors in determining how significant these reactions are in the formation of the ozone hole over Antarctica.
